Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions about Exhibit B caps/floors application across SKUs

Evelyn,

Thanks for the redlines on the Order Form. Our procurement team ran the revised Exhibit B by finance and they're asking for clarification on a corner case that matters to our billing processes. Specifically: when multiple SKUs from Schedule A are billed in the same period, do the "protection bands" (caps/floors) apply (a) per individual SKU, (b) aggregated across the account, or (c) on a blended basis using the SKU list prices?

Example that prompted this: if SKU-A (data+inference) has a floor of $5k and SKU-B (support/ops) has a floor of $2k, and we invoice $4k SKU-A + $3k SKU-B, does the floor trigger happen? Our accounting system flattens SKUs into buckets and we need clear contract language to map to invoicing.

Can you confirm which interpretation Redwood intends? If you can provide a short mapping we can give to our billing team, that would speed procurement. We attached your latest Exhibit B for reference.

—Alyssa

Alyssa — thanks for the concrete example, that helps. Short answer: Redwood's commercial intent is to protect against volatility at the invoice level, not to create per-SKU "islands" that can be gamed. Practically speaking we believe the contract should read that caps/floors apply to the aggregated invoice amount for the applicable billing period across SKUs covered by the same Order Form.

That said, I want to run this by Finance and Legal so we give you a defensible clause. I've drafted a one-page operational mapping (see attached pricing-band-matrix.xlsx) that shows how to translate invoices into the "aggregate" calculation and how a blended fallback would work if one SKU is treated differently for regulatory/billing reasons.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll route the mapping to Finance (Karthik) and Legal (Marissa) for quick confirmation.
- If Lumen is comfortable with aggregate application, we'll send a narrow redline to Exhibit B that replaces the current per-SKU wording.
- If you prefer per-SKU language, we can provide a short technical addendum for invoicing automation.

Are you available for a 20-minute call tomorrow to lock this?

Evelyn — looping Finance/Revenue Ops. I reviewed the attached matrix. Operational note from our side: our billing system (LedgerBX) supports both per-SKU and account-aggregate calculations, but the revenue recognition and reporting differ. If we apply the bands at the aggregate invoice level we must ensure: 

- Revenue recognition rules are agreed (we'll provide an example journal entry).
- Partner/third-party pass-through SKUs are excluded by explicit list (we can't treat pass-throughs as contributing to the protection band).
- For mixed invoices, we need a deterministic tie-breaker; the matrix's "blended fallback" makes sense but must be encoded.

I attached a short invoice mapping that shows how an invoice like Alyssa's example would be normalized, the math to check floors, and how credits/true-ups would appear on the next invoice. Laura/legal — please advise whether we need contract-level language around exclusion lists and whether a defined "invoice normalization" process should be included in Exhibit B.

—Karthik

Subject: Re: Interpretation and billing mapping for pricing protection bands — LumenHealth

Team — quick legal read and recommendation. Goal is to avoid ambiguity and reduce month-to-month disputes. Suggested contract language (high level):

1) "Aggregate Application": "Unless otherwise specified in Schedule A, Pricing Protection Bands ("Bands") shall be applied to the aggregate invoice value for the applicable billing period across all SKUs covered by the same Order Form."

2) "Exclusions and Pass-Throughs": "The Parties may agree in writing to exclude certain SKUs from the aggregate calculation (e.g., third-party pass-throughs). Any such exclusions must be enumerated in Schedule A and may be updated by mutual written consent."

3) "Invoice Normalization and Dispute Window": "Invoices will be normalized according to the invoice normalization procedure attached as Annex 1 to Exhibit B. Disputes about Band calculations must be raised within thirty (30) days of invoice issuance. Adjustments, if any, will be processed on the next invoice period."

The above preserves the aggregate intent but creates a clean on-ramp for exclusion lists and a binding normalization process (which helps ops). If Lumen agrees to this structure, I can produce a redline that replaces the existing paragraph in Exhibit B and adds a one-paragraph Annex with a worked example.

If Lumen insists on strict per-SKU floors, we should reserve the right to require automation mapping costs and include an implementation SOW; otherwise it's an ops burden.

—Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

- Principle: Bands are applied to the aggregate invoice amount for SKUs on the same Order Form.
- Exclusions: Third-party pass-through SKUs are explicitly excluded; those SKUs must be listed in Schedule A.
- Annex: Invoice normalization procedure will be appended to Exhibit B (one page) with the worked example you provided.
- Disputes: 30-day dispute window; adjustments to be reflected on the next invoice.
